claim: B1 gives at least 400 mL/min at a comfortable adult squeeze (17 kPa) with a clean module in 20 C water
law: Darcy flux J = Lp x TMP over 0.174 m2 of outside fibre area, assumed clean-water permeability 1,000 L/(m2 h bar), a quarter of the 0.1 um PVDF example in US 8,708,161 B2; Ergun bed, Hagen-Poiseuille lumens and outlet in series (CAL section 3); fouled 242, at 10 C 360 mL/min (S31)
check: 465 mL/min >= 400 mL/min

claim: B1 gives at least 150 mL/min at a weak child's squeeze (5.8 kPa, girls' boundary 11.8 kg) and an elderly woman's (7.2 kPa) with a clean module in 20 C water
law: As S1 at the persona pressures; assumed clean-water permeability 1,000 L/(m2 h bar), a quarter of the 0.1 um PVDF example in US 8,708,161 B2; fouled 82, at 10 C 123 mL/min (S31)
check: 160 mL/min >= 150 mL/min

claim: A hand squeeze on a 1 L PET bottle gives about 6 to 17 kPa held and about 43 kPa at full grip
law: Grip norms (Camry dynamometer, 10 to 11 years and 70 to 99 years) x 40 % held x 0.8 wall loss over an 80 x 80 mm contact; STANDARDS 25.6 range 10 to 30 kPa
check: Model only: the dynamometer grip is not the grip on an 80 mm cylinder (a diameter factor of about 0.6 would give 10 kPa for the adult) and a child's hand does not wrap 80 mm; two-handed squeezing is the design case; bottle pressure to measure with a gauge (HWP-VER-001 TH)

claim: Mesh, carbon bed, lumens and outlet together take under a fifth of the squeeze pressure, so the membrane sets the flow
law: Pressure drop per stage at the adult squeeze: Ergun bed (12 x 40 GAC, void 0.40), lumens, nipple, nozzle and valve ports; clean bed only, silt loading is S32

claim: Flux arithmetic: 1,000 L/(m2 h bar) x 0.174 m2 at 10 kPa is about 290 mL/min before the other stages
law: L/(m2 h bar) x m2 x bar = L/h; / 60 x 1000 = mL/min
check: claimed 289.864 mL/min, estimate 274 mL/min (ratio 1.06)

claim: B2 gravity drip treats 1 L in under 15 minutes with a clean module in 20 C water (heads 2.5 to 5.2 kPa)
law: Falling-head drain of an inverted 1 L bottle through 0.295 m2; assumed clean-water permeability 1,000 L/(m2 h bar), a quarter of the 0.1 um PVDF example in US 8,708,161 B2
check: 6.2 min per litre clean, 11.9 min fouled, against 15 min; at 10 C 8.1 and 15.6 min; rests on the assumed permeability (supplier flux data, HWB-DEC-001 C1)

claim: B3 press reaches 18 kPa with 80 N of arm or body weight and gives at least 300 mL/min with a clean module
law: p = (F - lip seal friction 10 N, assumed; 30 N would give 13 kPa) / cup bore area (70 mm); flow as S1
check: 500 mL/min clean, 257 fouled, against 300; rests on the assumed permeability

claim: B3 press tube holds the 350 mL fill line of treated water above and around the cartridge
law: Press tube volume less the cartridge housing volume

claim: A 0.1 um hollow-fibre membrane is a size barrier for protozoan cysts (about 3 to 15 um) and is designed to reduce most bacteria; no removal is claimed from the pore label
law: Size exclusion: Cryptosporidium oocysts 4 to 6 um, Giardia cysts 8 to 12 um (40 to 120 x the 0.1 um pore); most bacteria are 0.3 um or more across, but thin forms such as Leptospira (about 0.1 um) reach the nominal pore; CDC: microfiltration very high effectiveness for protozoa, moderate for bacteria
check: Sieving ratio about 1 for the thinnest bacteria and 3 for Brevundimonas diminuta (0.3 um), so the pore label is not a bacteria barrier; the supplier's absolute rating (C1) and an accredited log reduction (HWP-VER-001 TA, TB) decide

claim: The membrane is not a virus barrier, so the product carries the no-virus warning and pairs with chlorine (solution D) where viruses are a risk
law: Viruses about 0.02 to 0.3 um overlap and pass a 0.1 um pore (sieving ratio 0.2 to 3); CDC: microfiltration not effective for viruses
check: No virus claim (Amish, 2026-11-11: no virus claim, co-treat); HWP-CLM-001 warning on the product

claim: The carbon capsule holds about 7 g of 12 x 40 coconut GAC
law: Bed 29.8 mm x 20 mm = 13.9 mL x bulk density 0.48 to 0.50 g/cm3 (Newterra 5DCAW 1240 data sheet)
check: claimed 7 g, estimate 6.84 g (ratio 1.02)

claim: Carbon intended to reduce chlorine taste at an empty-bed contact time of 1.8 to 5.2 s (B1) and about 5 s (B2)
law: EBCT = bed volume / flow; the true residence time is about 0.4 x EBCT (void 0.40); seconds of contact are short for granular carbon (concept validation questions, item 19); free chlorine reacts fast at carbon surfaces, organics and odours much more slowly
check: Chlorine taste reduction is a target only, no odour or organics claim, to measure with an NSF/ANSI 42 style test and a breakthrough curve that sets the capsule life (HWP-VER-001 TG); 150 L capsule life is assumed

claim: Squeezing air through the wetted cartridge (empty bottle) shows a broken fibre as a stream of bubbles, while an intact 0.1 um membrane holds air
law: Young-Laplace bubble point dP = 4 gamma / d: 0.1 um pore about 2,900 kPa ideal (real membranes lower, still far above 17 kPa); open 0.5 mm lumen 0.6 kPa; adult squeeze 17 kPa with the outlet in a cup of water reveals any opening above about 17 um

claim: The air test, done with an adult squeeze, does not find round defects under about 17 um (slits under about 9 um), so it is a check for gross damage, not proof of pathogen performance
law: Bubble point at the available squeeze: d = 4 gamma / dP = 17 um at 17 kPa (slit width 2 gamma / dP = 8.5 um); a weak user's 6 kPa finds only openings above about 50 um; cysts are 4 to 15 um, bacteria 0.1 to 5 um
check: User guidance says 'stop using if bubbles stream'; never 'safe if no bubbles'. Production integrity test by the module maker (TI)

claim: Wet fibres can be damaged by freezing without any change in flow, so the product carries a do-not-freeze-wet warning and a retire-after-freezing rule
law: Water expands about 9 % on freezing; competitors report freezing as the main silent-failure cause (concept validation questions, item 17)
check: No freeze claim; warning and pictogram; air test after suspected freezing; retire if frozen wet (HWP-VER-001 TF)

claim: The housing stays far below the strength of printed polypropylene at the highest squeeze and a hard backflush
law: Hoop p r / t and the flat 4 mm end wall as a circular plate (1.24 p a2 / t2, simply supported); printed PP taken at 10 MPa (assumed, a third of moulded PP yield; layer strength lower)
check: Full squeeze: end wall 1.14 MPa, factor 9. Backflush as instructed (collar end open): shell near 0 kPa. If the collar end were blocked at 179 kPa: hoop 1.65 MPa but end wall 4.7 MPa, factor 2.1 against PR-028's 5 (6.2 mm wall needed; HWB-DEC-001 D8); burst test at TRL 4

claim: A 60 mL syringe backflush (54 kPa gentle to 179 kPa hard) stays inside the module's backwash limit
law: p = F / syringe bore area (26.7 mm); the module maker's maximum backwash pressure is not yet known
check: To confirm from the supplier (HWB-DEC-001 C2), with the potting bond rated for 135 N at 179 kPa; the instruction is a gentle push; backflush runs with the carbon capsule removed so no fines or carbon are flushed into the fibres

claim: Wet carbon downstream of the membrane (the briefed B1 layout) would grow bacteria on the clean side in warm storage and need a backflush bypass
law: Carbon after the membrane can harbour microorganisms (Rev A specification section 05); wet carbon supports regrowth (concept validation questions, item 21)
check: Failed as briefed, fixed: carbon moved to a dirty-side capsule upstream of the membrane, so the membrane is the last barrier and backflush never passes carbon

claim: On release the squeezed bottle refills with air without unscrewing
law: A wetted 0.1 um membrane blocks air up to its bubble point (about 2,900 kPa, S13), so air cannot return through the outlet; a dirty-side duckbill valve opens inward at about 0.5 kPa (assumed) and closes under squeeze; tipped, it sits under the bottle's water and needs about 2.9 kPa of vacuum
check: Failed as briefed (no air path), fixed with a duckbill valve in the collar (F2); the bottle is turned upright on release so the valve is in air and opens at about 0.5 kPa (F5); springback of a thin still-water bottle to confirm by test (TH)

claim: The B2 stand does not tip over when the full bottle hangs in it
law: Tip angle atan(base radius / centre of gravity height) for the continuous base ring (not leg feet) with a full 1 L bottle; criterion 15 deg (assumed); base radius 65 mm gave 9.9 deg (failed), widened to 115 mm; a 4.4 N side push at the centre of gravity still tips it, so the stand goes on a table away from children's reach
check: 17.2 deg >= 15 deg

claim: The inverted bottle of B2 drains without collapsing or locking
law: Air must replace the water leaving the bottle; the wetted membrane blocks air (S13). The 4 x 0.8 vent tube has a 2.4 mm bore (Bond number 0.77, below 3.37), so water it takes in on filling stays as a plug that the bottle must purge
check: Failed as briefed, fixed with the vent tube (F4); the first purge needs about 2.9 kPa of bottle vacuum against a 5.2 kPa full head, so it works on paper with a slow first minute; to confirm by test (TH)

claim: With carbon on the dirty side, the clean side holds about 21 mL: 5.7 mL in the header, nipple and spout, which drains, and 15.2 mL in the lumens, which stays wet; a first flush after storage clears it
law: Biofilm grows where water stands on wetted surfaces; capillary rise in a 0.5 mm lumen is about 60 mm, so the lumens never drain; bacteria can grow through 0.1 to 0.2 um membranes over days of wet storage; the outlet can be recontaminated by the mouth or hands
check: Refuted as first stated ('drains and dries', 5.7 mL), fixed: discard the first 50 mL after any storage (F6); grow-through and regrowth to measure in storage cycles (HWP-VER-001 TE, TG); dust cover, pour into a cup for shared use

claim: Every wetted material is from a family available in NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 grades: PP, EPDM or silicone, 316L, PVDF or PES fibres, polyurethane or epoxy potting, coconut GAC
law: NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 and 372 set the contact-material references; printed prototype parts are not certified
check: Extractables and leachables of the actual grades, potting (residual isocyanate or amine) and carbon fines and ash (TG); the first flush (F6) also clears fines; prototypes are used with known potable test water only

claim: One collar fits both 28 mm PCO 1881 and PCO 1810 necks: the skirt clears the support ring of the shorter 1881 neck
law: Same thread diameter and pitch (about 27.4 mm, 2.7 mm); neck height about 17 mm (1881) and 21 mm (1810); skirt 15.5 mm below the lip with the compressed 1.5 mm gasket included (Kapy CAD, approximate); thread starts and tolerances from the ISBT drawings (C7)
check: 1.5 mm >= 1 mm

claim: A printed adapter fits the collar to 38 mm two-start necks used on wide-mouth juice and dairy bottles
law: 38 mm two-start finishes exist in several variants (Bericap 38 mm HF two-start; Petainer 38 mm two-start)
check: Dimensions of the exact 38 mm finish to obtain from its drawing before the adapter is drawn (HWB-DEC-001 C4)

claim: The B1 cartridge weighs about 120 g dry and about 182 g wet
law: Model volumes x densities (PP 905, EPDM 1,150, 316L 7,950 kg/m3, fibres 30 % solid PVDF, GAC 490 kg/m3)
check: claimed 120 g, estimate 118 g (ratio 1.02)

claim: A weak child can fill a 250 mL cup in about 94 s of squeezing with a clean module, in short squeezes
law: Held grip of 40 % of maximum is assumed for 10 to 20 s at a time; the fouled module halves the flow (183 s); a litre takes a weak child 6 min clean; household volumes are B2's job
check: Persona trials with known potable water only (HWP-VER-001 TH); if children cannot sustain it, B2 gravity is the household mode

claim: Chlorine co-treatment works with the cartridge only if the water is dosed and left for solution D's full contact time before it is filtered; the filtered water then carries no residual
law: Granular carbon removes free chlorine within seconds (S12), so the CT stops at the carbon; WHO and solution D set the dose and contact time (about 30 min) in the bottle; nothing downstream protects stored water
check: Fixed: dose, wait, then filter; drink or use the filtered water the same day and do not store it (F7); the pictogram shows the order (PR-003)

claim: The only dirty-to-clean routes, the header O-rings and the potting, are free of bypass at 53 % fibre packing
law: Packing 53 % of the header bore (800 fibre ends of 0.8 mm in 31 mm); above about 50 % potting may not penetrate fully and leave voids; a gap under 17 um (slit 8.5 um) passes cysts and bacteria and is not seen by the air test (S14)
check: Supplier to confirm packing, potting penetration and a production integrity test of every module (C1, F9); assembled-cartridge challenge (HWP-VER-001 TA, TB); about 300 U fibres (0.13 m2, flows about 25 % lower) if the maker asks for less

claim: The bought fibres pass water at a few kPa
law: Plain PVDF is hydrophobic: water enters a 0.1 um pore only far above 17 kPa; hydrophilised PVDF or PES passes water but can dewet if it dries out
check: Fixed in the module request: hydrophilic PVDF or PES, shipped wet or with a wetting agent (F9); first-use priming and a backflush if first flow is low (F8)

claim: Every flow figure is for 20 C water; cold water gives about a quarter less
law: Flux and laminar losses scale with 1 / viscosity: 1.00 mPa s at 20 C, 1.31 at 10 C (0.77 x)
check: At 10 C: adult 360 mL/min clean (under PR-004's 400), weak child 123 and elderly woman 152 (PR-005's 150); B2 15.6 min per litre fouled. Rating temperature is HWB-DEC-001 D9

claim: The upstream carbon bed keeps its flow in turbid water
law: The 150 um mesh passes silt, so the carbon bed works as a depth filter and cannot be backflushed (capsule out); Ergun viscous loss rises about 3.4 x as bed voids fall from 0.40 to 0.30
check: Settle or cloth-filter turbid water first (HWP-SRC-001); replace the capsule when a backflush does not restore the flow (instructions, PR-016); clog rate to measure (HWP-VER-001 TE)

claim: Air left on the dirty side does not blind the fibres
law: Air in the shell cannot cross the wetted membrane (S13) and rises against the flow through a wet 12 x 40 bed only above a capillary entry of about 1 to 2 kPa; at B2's 2.5 to 5 kPa head it may stay and cover fibres
check: Fixed: prime at first use and after drying by a syringe backflush with the capsule out, which fills the shell from the fibres outward and pushes the air out of the open collar end (F8); to confirm by test (TC)
